what: Stop the api.request logging middleware from buffering and re-parsing response bodies, and stream /api/entries item by item from a database cursor, so a full-content 10,000-item request costs about what a slim one does.
why: Design: docs/work/bounded-list-memory/design.md. Found on real use 2026-10-10: an old TUI on bishop requested the full 10,000-item list and cerebro peaked at 2.9 GB of 3.9 GB; measured locally on a copy of cerebro's database, that request peaks at 2,954 MB against 642 MB for the slim view.

criteria.given: a test database with items of every priority, some with long content and analysis
criteria.when: /api/entries is requested with view=full and view=list, with and without filters, sort options, since and skip_dedup=false
criteria.then: it fails if any response body differs from the body the previous dict construction produced for the same request; otherwise every body is identical, and the test is shown red with one per-item field dropped from the stream

criteria.given: a request that fails validation (an invalid priority, an invalid since)
criteria.then: it fails if the response is not the same 4xx JSON envelope as before; otherwise it is
it fails if the middleware reads the response body or the logged item_count is missing or wrong; otherwise item_count matches the number of items sent, read from request state

criteria.given: the committed memory probe and a copy of cerebro's database
criteria.when: the probe runs the full and the slim 10,000-item requests through the app in separate processes
criteria.then: it fails if the full request's peak RSS exceeds the slim request's by more than 100 MB; otherwise it is within 100 MB, with the before and after figures recorded beside the work order
it fails on any failing check; otherwise its last line is `verify: PASS`

outOfScope: An error after the stream has started (a database failure mid-cursor) can only end the stream early, not change the status code; such a response is truncated JSON the client fails to parse rather than a clean 500.
Responses are sent chunked without a Content-Length.
stakes: A full-content GET /api/entries?limit=10000 on a copy of cerebro's database peaks within 100 MB of the view=list request, down from 2,954 MB.

The JSON a client receives from /api/entries is unchanged for view=full and view=list: same envelope, same items in the same order, same fields and values, proven by a test that compares against the previous construction.
The logging middleware reads no response body, and api.request events keep item_count for /api/entries and /api/search.
Deduplication, filters, sorting, limits and errors behave as before: a validation error still returns the same 4xx envelope, not a broken stream.
After deploy, cerebro's memory peak stays under 1.5 GB through a full-list request from an old client.
